events.title: The Restorer's Statue
events.desc: Selen's square has a new statue of Harion the Restorer, cast in the foundry by the river and set up on a plinth of Selen limestone. It is taller than any statue of a king in Parim. The sculptor was told to make him a Selen man first and a king second, and the statue's boots have mud on them.

options.name: Let Parim see it.
options.tip: Parim will not like to be looked down on.

events.title: Ents Count the Rings
events.desc: The ents have counted the rings of the oldest tree in the forest again. They lost count, and began again. They have been counting for as long as there have been ents, and the trouble is, they say, that the tree keeps growing.

events.title: The Giants' Fair
events.desc: Giants come down to the lake for the fair, wading in to the thigh, and the merchants of the little towns sell them boots that are never big enough. The giants buy them every year and wear them as hats. Everyone agrees that this is the best part of the fair.

events.title: Horse Fair at Hunhun
events.desc: At the riders' horse fair a lord of Parim offers too little for the best stallion and is laughed home. The stallion belongs to a girl of fourteen, who has refused three offers and has asked the price of the horse's name.

events.title: Gate Day at Kingson
events.desc: Once a year the great gate in the Wall stands open from dawn to dusk, and elves and men trade in its shadow without a toll. The custom is older than the Accord and has outlived two attempts to end it. The gate-wardens stand on either side in their ceremonial plain wool.

options.name: Keep the old custom.
options.tip: The Magical Forest will think well of Kingson.

events.title: Every Envoy Returned
events.desc: The Veiled Elder sent back every envoy of the year with their letters unopened. The envoys were fed, lodged and sent home with presents. Not one of them could say afterwards what the Elder looked like, or whether the Elder was a man or a woman.

options.name: We wish to be left alone.

desc.text: Our young men raided a farm across the border. The farmer's dog bit one of them, which the others are not allowing him to forget. The raid was a success, in the sense that nobody was killed and a goat was taken.

Raiders from the Bloody Forest burned a barn on our border. They took a goat and left a message in blood on the door, which the barn's owner has been scrubbing for a day. It said, in a bad hand, that they would be back.

events.title: The First Port
events.desc: Asgard remembers that its harbour was the first the Aenoran ships reached, long ago. The houses on the quay still keep the day, with bunting in the shape of the old square sails. The children are told that the first sailors were all hungry, and that it was Asgard's grandmothers who fed them.

events.title: Between Two Masters
events.desc: Sonargur and Parim both sent envoys this month. Each asked for the same thing, which was nothing in particular, and each wanted it written down. The seal-keeper of Molot has drafted two replies in identical words and is trying to decide which seal goes on which.

events.title: The Gateway Toll
events.desc: Ships between the Leren and the Aenoran seas pay R'en's toll at the gateway of the strait, and captains from both seas complain of it in the same words. The toll-keeper has begun to keep a list of the complaints. It is longer than the list of the dues.

events.title: The Long Hunt
events.desc: The yeti of the white valleys go on the long hunt in the dead of the year. They come back with more than they need, and they share it. The elders say that this is the whole of their law, and that other people's laws are longer but do not do more.

events.title: The Frost-King's Riddle
events.desc: The Frost-King sets a riddle for every envoy. Nobody has answered it in a hundred years, and the envoys have stopped trying. They tell the Frost-King that the answer is a secret, and he nods gravely, and all agree that this is the best answer that has been offered.

events.title: The Windwaith Regatta
events.desc: The sea-city races its ships round the capes. Coldor's captains lose again, as they have every year since the race began, and send a barrel of their best to the winners with a note that says only: next year.

desc.text: Another fort rises on the march, of grey stone dragged by oxen from the old quarries. The masons sing at their work. The Refusal of 850 is not mentioned in the songs, and is the reason for all of them.

Isengard builds another fort on the march. The watchtower at the border has counted eleven since the last thaw, and the garrison's commander has asked whether the count is a boast or a threat. Nobody at the Winter Court is sure.

events.title: Companies for Hire
events.desc: The Buldor companies look for contracts. In a year of peace the only buyers are merchants who want guards, and the captains are learning what it is to be hired by a man who cares whether the wagons arrive with their wheels on.

events.title: The Guild Strike
events.desc: Kradlon's guilds stop the forges for a week over Aenoran tariffs on their iron. The apprentices sit on the cold anvils and the masters stand with their arms folded. The city has gone quiet in a way it has not been quiet in living memory, and the sound is not restful.

events.title: Ledger Day in Corogon
events.desc: The trading city opens its ledgers to the townsfolk once a year, and they come with their own books to compare. This year, for the first time in anyone's memory, they balance. The treasurer has had to sit down.

events.title: Storm Season in the Pupor Ocean
events.desc: The autumn storms came early. Two charts were wrong, and one was wrong in a way that the chart-masters will not discuss in front of the apprentices. A fishing fleet came home a week late and a boat short, with a story about a current that the charts do not show.

events.title: Blackton's Free Market
events.desc: Orcs, men and goblins trade in Blackton's market under one rule: no blades drawn. The rule is chalked on the gate in four scripts. Last winter a goblin stallholder pulled a knife on an orc who had insulted his scales, and was thrown out of the market by the other goblins, who were embarrassed.

events.title: The Troll Bridge Toll
events.desc: Travellers through the Troll Forest pay at the old bridge. The trolls take payment in iron, not gold, and are unmoved by arguments about the relative value. A merchant has been trying for an hour to persuade them that his gold is heavier than their iron.

desc.text: The grove songs this year name an old slight from Andos Enda. It is a very old slight, and the song is a very long one, and the young singers have to be reminded of the second verse.
Herrodon is singing about us again. The grove songs this year name an old slight, and the singers have found a rhyme for Andos Enda that the elders consider uncalled for.

options.name: Sing louder.
options.tip: Andos Enda will not like it.

events.title: Wardens of the High Passes
events.desc: Nolorim's pass-wardens change the guard on the high road, as they have every spring for ages. The old guard hands the new one a staff and a lantern and a list of the names of those who have passed since autumn. The list is short.

events.title: The Mushroom Forest Blooms
events.desc: The giant mushrooms bloomed in one night, and the glow could be seen from the Wall. Watchmen on the towers took it for a fire and rang the bells, and the elves of the forest came out with lanterns to put it out. They found nothing burning.

events.title: The Holy Breeze
events.desc: The breeze from the sea that Olen calls holy blew for nine days this summer, and the washing dried in an hour. The priests of the breeze held a procession on the tenth day, at which several people were seen to be weeping with relief at having their shirts back.

events.title: The Warlord's Games
events.desc: Nan's warlord holds games. The winners join his guard, and the losers are given a meal and a place on the benches. The crowd is large, and the warlord is said to be paying more attention to the losers' faces than to the winners'.

events.title: The Lake Assembly
events.desc: Mora's lake towns send their speakers to the assembly. It argues for a month about fishing rights, and ends by passing the same rule it passed last year, with a clause added about nets.

events.title: Red Banners
events.desc: Avalon's revolutionaries celebrate the anniversary of the day they threw out their lords, marching through the streets under red banners, and the neighbouring kings close their borders for a day. The marchers consider this the best compliment of the year.

events.title: The Rice Harvest
events.desc: The rice terraces of Howan gave a double harvest, and there was not enough room in the granaries to hold it. The village headmen stood about the heaped sacks like men who have been given too much change.

events.title: The Canoe Race
events.desc: The islands race their canoes across the strait. Both claim the victory, and both can show the judge a witness who saw the other's canoe turn back. The judge has been rowing between the islands for two days with a cup that neither will take.

events.title: The Noon Festival
events.desc: At noon on the longest day the tall folk gather in silence to watch the sun stand still. A child coughs, and the whole assembly turns its head, and then the sun moves on, and nobody is certain which of them it was waiting for.

events.title: Pilgrims to the Sea of Gods
events.desc: Pilgrims walk to the shore of the Sea of Gods to throw flowers on the water. They go in a line, barefoot, with baskets, and they do not speak. The tide carries the flowers a little way out and brings some of them back.

events.title: Black Ribbons in the Market
events.desc: The markets are hung with black ribbons, and the cloth merchants have never sold so much. In the Great Lake ports the fishermen row out at dawn with a black cloth on the prow, and the harbour bells ring once, very slowly, for a king that few of them could have named at a feast.

events.title: Hymns for the God-King
events.desc: The temples sing new hymns: [zin_loc_deliverer] wears Aenor's crown. The choirs have learned them in a week from copies carried by couriers in grey cloaks, and the old women, who prefer the old ones, sing the new ones a little more slowly.

options.name: Our court keeps its own hymns.

events.title: Songs of the Grey Ford
events.desc: Bards sing of the war-king who made the peace at the Grey Ford and gave the crown back. They call him the King Without a House, and no bard knows more of him than the verse. The song is short, and the bards say that this is because the man was.

events.title: Silence at the Castle
events.desc: Traders say that the lord of the silent castle in the north is dead. A warden keeps its gates now, and nobody goes in. The warden is said to be courteous to travellers, and to give them water, and to ask them to go no farther.

events.title: Bread Doubles in Price
events.desc: The price of bread has doubled in a season. The bakers say it is the carters, the carters say it is the millers, and the millers say it is the wars, and nobody who has worked it out has been able to make the sums come to less.

events.title: Swords for Hire
events.desc: Every company in the West has a contract now. Some have two. The recruiting-captains of the great houses have taken to waiting outside the tavern doors of the companies' captains, with purses.

events.title: Empty Villages on the Coast
events.desc: The fishing villages of the north coast are empty. The fishermen were right, and have gone inland with their nets in carts, and the cats of the villages sit on the doorsteps and look at the sea.

events.title: Broken Images
events.desc: In the night someone broke the Deliverer's image at the temple door. In the morning the poor still came for bread, and found it, and stood a little apart from the broken stone as they ate, as at the grave of a relative they have only now learned they disliked.

events.title: The Storms Thin

all: NOT = { AND = { is_subject = yes OVERLORD = { zin_is_volgan = yes } } }

events.desc: Sailors say the storms over the south are thinner this season, and that a ship can stand in to the old coast for half a day before the sky closes. Nobody knows what it means. The masters have begun to chart the gaps.

events.title: White Banners in the South
events.desc: The towers of the south hang white banners for the King of Gala. Nobody in the sun-realms has been asked to, and every tower has done it on the same morning. Old men who were children when he last came north stand in the squares with their hats in their hands.

events.title: Refugees Come Home
events.desc: The roads to the Great Lake are full again, this time going home. Families walk with their bedding on their backs, past the villages where they used to buy bread, and stop to look at the doors that are still standing.

events.title: Bells for a New King
events.desc: Bells ring in Parim for a king of Aen's line. In our own streets, people argue whether that is good news, and the arguments run along the oldest lines of the quarrel: those who say that a king is a king, and those who say that Aen's line has not been good for the West.

options.name: It is.
options.tip: Aenor will think well of us.

events.title: A Dragon Leaves the Roosts
events.desc: A dragon has left the high roosts with a rider. The roost wardens say it went of its own will, and that no one asked it to, and they have the claw-marks on the ledge to show it. The elder of the roosts has gone out to the ledge and is sitting there alone.

events.title: The Wall Without Its Watch
events.desc: Half the Wall's watchtowers are empty. The garrisons went to Parim, or east, or home. The gatehouse is manned by an old gate-captain and his grandson, who is learning to light the beacons.

events.title: Ships in Every Harbour
events.desc: Every hull that can float has been hired for the western crossing. Our harbours are empty and our purses full. The chart-masters have been paid to draw the central sea three times over, and each time to a different scale.
